page: Microsoft Azure EC16as_v5 is a memory-optimized instance designed for enterprise applications demanding high memory capacity relative to compute resources. Hosted on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, it provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores via two threads per core on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning totals 128.0 GB, resulting in an 8.0 GB per-core density. Cache hierarchy features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. In terms of hardware capabilities, the processor incorporates AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic and bit manipulation flags, while omitting AVX-512 extensions. The server does not bundle local disk storage and includes zero GPUs, requiring attached network volumes for persistent storage needs.

Benchmark evaluations place the computational and memory throughput of the instance firmly within the average band across peer systems. Single-core evaluation via stress-ng registered 1992.87, expanding to 15873.19 under multi-core stress testing. Geekbench measurements returned a single-core score of 1210.0 and a multi-core score of 7343.0, with sub-tests registering 11685.0 for Clang software compilation and 13966.0 for ray tracing. PassMark testing further validated this mid-tier baseline with an overall CPU score of 17013.38, a memory rating of 2084.53, and a database operations mark of 5673.51. In memory-dependent transactional benchmarking, the system sustained 13.52 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio offers a cost-effective allocation for workloads constrained by RAM rather than raw computing cycles. Because the instance contains no complimentary local NVMe or SSD capacity, storage performance relies on external disk integration, which represents an architectural tradeoff for high-IOPS temporary disk use cases. The configuration matches environments such as Redis or Memcached in-memory caching, relational and operational databases, large-scale software compilation pipelines, and transactional enterprise backends requiring steady compute paired with generous RAM.
description: Microsoft Azure EC16as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. Based on x86_64 architecture, the configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation, alongside 32 MB of L3 cache. The instance features no integrated local storage and contains zero GPUs, necessitating external storage volumes for stateful data persistence. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI extensions. In synthetic testing, the instance achieved 1,210.0 in Geekbench single-core, 7,343.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and 17,013.38 in PassMark CPU score, placing its compute and memory throughput consistently within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud hardware. Delivering 13.52 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, the server delivers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy setups such as in-memory data structures, caching layers, database instances, and enterprise backend platforms.
